name: Maria Dias
life: “I still remember a homework session interrupted by the night neighbor coming home.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Maria by a small Saturday habit. Maria knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I can rent a room to the lodger but I have a noisy night shift. We are trying a weekend first.
appearance: Maria is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Maria turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Maria finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To test the offered room through a night shift.
family: Malcolm Garrett is Maria’s second cousin. Maria offers the first invitation. Malcolm gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Malcolm says, “I paid for my license by cleaning the instructor's flat.”
connections: Roland Bloom. Trying a noisy room and keeping Thursday supper give the move an ordinary weekly rhythm.

reactions.situation: The lodger is asked to leave on short notice
reactions.response: Maria checks where the lodger can go before treating an empty room as a settled fact.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Maria stays with the rider after the people who saw the fall start drifting away.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Maria waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
